Sasha (eng-runtime): quick heads-up — I ran the nightly attention microbench across SM80/SM90 on both CUDA/native kernels and Triton Flash variants. seeing a ~12-18% drop on SM90/TRITON for seq>=1024 compared to SM80/CUDA fused kernel. weirdly small reg for seq=128.

Alex R: can you paste the bench command + outputs?

Sasha (eng-runtime): sure — command used: `./bench_attention --model gpt2 --bs 4 --seq 2048 --iters 200 --variant triton_flash_paged --device sm90`

bench stdout:
```
variant: cuda_fused_sm80  | seq=2048 | bs=4 | tokens/s = 980k  | p50 latency per token = 0.85ms
variant: triton_flash_paged_sm90 | seq=2048 | bs=4 | tokens/s = 824k  | p50 latency per token = 1.02ms
variant: triton_flash_fused_sm90 | seq=2048 | bs=4 | tokens/s = 810k  | p50 = 1.05ms
variant: cuda_fused_sm90 (native) | seq=2048 | bs=4 | tokens/s = 970k | p50 = 0.86ms
```
So Triton variants on SM90 are slower than native CUDA fused kernel on same arch. SM80/CUDA still fastest for this workload.

Maria (ML): interesting — is the Triton build using the same CUDA toolkit as the native kernel? mismatched nvcc flags can change codegen.

Sasha (eng-runtime): good catch. Triton was built against CUDA 12.4 (system), whereas our CUDA kernel was compiled with 12.1. Also TRITON_CUDA_ARCH was sm_90 in build. I tried rebuilding Triton with `-arch=sm_90` and `--use-warp-mma=false` (for testing) — small improvement but still ~8% gap.

Jay (SRE): can you share an `nsys` summary or kernel timeline? might be memory stalls or memcpy differences (KV cache behavior).

Sasha (eng-runtime): pasted simplified nsys flame stats below — selecting top GPU kernels by total time:
```
1) triton_attn_kernel (grid: 512x) - 46.2ms total - %gpu time 62% - l2_read_bytes high
2) cuda_fused_attn (grid: 64x) - 28.7ms total - %gpu time 38% - better shared mem reuse
3) memcpy_h2d/d2h - 5.1ms combined
4) triton_prefetch_stage - 8.4ms
```
Kernel-level counters: Triton kernel shows ~2.5x L2 read transactions and higher warp_serialize/stall_due_to_memory. Suggests less efficient tiling / reuse on SM90 codepath.

Liam (infra): any difference in hw config? same GPU model? driver version?

Sasha (eng-runtime): both runs used A100-80C (SM90) and A100-40C (SM80) respectively in different hosts. Driver on SM90 host is 535.86, SM80 host 525.x. I also repeated SM90 with driver 525.x in a compatibility test — Triton still slower but gap shrinks to ~9%. So driver plays a role but not full story.

Alex R: could this be due to our batching heuristic + KV cache layout? If Triton kernel expects packed KV layout and our runtime is doing incremental memcpy for variable-length batches, that could kill perf at long seqs.

Sasha (eng-runtime): I instrumented RPC path: we do per-request KV prefetch when cache miss + pad to 64 for alignment. For Triton run I observed extra `cudaMemcpyAsync` calls per step (see below):
```
[step 1] cudaMemcpyAsync(kv_host->kv_dev, size=96MB)
[step 1] launch triton_attn_kernel
[step 1] cudaMemcpyAsync(kv_dev->kv_cache->hotswap, 1MB)
```
That extra copy doesn't happen on native fused path because it uses a persistent device allocation and writes directly into tiled buffers.

Maria (ML): can you run with `--disable_kv_prefetch` or `--persist_kv` options? If problem disappears, then it's KV copy pattern + kernel semantics mismatch.

Sasha (eng-runtime): ran `--persist_kv` (keep KV on device) — Triton throughput improved to 920k tokens/s for seq=2048 (down only ~5% vs cuda_fused_sm80). So KV memcpy was a big part. With persist_kv + rebuild Triton w/ CUDA 12.1 got parity within noise.

Jay (SRE): great find. But we can't require persist_kv for everyone — need to make kernel + runtime play nice by default. Options: 1) change batching heuristic to coalesce similar-length sequences to reduce extra memcpys; 2) update Triton kernel to accept our hot-swap layout (so it doesn't copy); 3) change allocator to pre-allocate per-stream KV buffer.

Liam (infra): also check Triton autotuning flags — sometimes it picks suboptimal tile sizes for SM90. We should run Triton's kernel selector with `TRITON_CONSERVE_SHARED_MEM=1` and `TRITON_FORCE_TILING=...` to force alternatives.

Alex R: another data point — fused attention (our custom CUDA) uses a different warp-level GEMM path that benefits from higher SM clock on SM80 in our infra. On SM90 that path is less efficient due to MMA instruction mapping. So pure kernel algorithmic differences matter.

Sasha (eng-runtime): logged follow-up perf-bot summary:
perf-bot: detected regressions in nightly: 2026-03-15 — attention_triton_paged — median -14% for seq>=1024 on SM90. correlated with Triton build against CUDA 12.4 and runtime KV prefetch.

Maria (ML): recommended action plan:
- Short term: enable `persist_kv` by default for long sequences in runtime (config flag per route).
- Medium: add runtime heuristic to coalesce same-seq-length requests to avoid per-request memcpys.
- Long term: upstream Triton kernel changes (tile/read pattern) or add an alternate CUDA kernel variant for SM90 (uses warp-mma-friendly tiling).

Sasha (eng-runtime): I've opened a PR with a runtime toggle + benchmark harness to validate defaults: `GG-3912` (WIP). Also attaching reproduction script in bench repo so perf team can run on internal clusters.

Alex R: I'll start a Triton repro with different `--max_shmem` and repro flags + try CUDA 12.1/12.4 builds. I'll also create a quick A/B job across SM80/SM90 to collect more stats (nsys + `nvtx` regions).

Jay (SRE): FYI I'll pin a canary with `persist_kv=true` for a small set of customer routes to observe any infra impacts.

Sasha (eng-runtime): TL;DR: regression on SM90 Triton Flash variants mostly due to KV memcpy pattern + Triton tiling choices + CUDA/toolkit mismatch. Mitigations: persist KV, rebuild Triton with matching CUDA, and tweak batching heuristics.

Liam (infra): nice triage. add this to the weekly perf sync and label root cause as `kv-copy + triton-tiling` for now. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: benchmark artifacts uploaded -> s3://redwood-perf/attention/1779123456/ (nsys traces + bench csv)

Sasha (eng-runtime): will follow up with PR links and perf dashboards once CI finishes. thanks all. :rocket:
